result.title: VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction
result.summary: Visual agents must turn video observations into timely decisions to track progress and choose what to do next. Building on the emerging System One paradigm, we introduce VideoJev, a family of models that cast video understanding and interaction as structured decision tasks. We adapt pretrained multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by replacing autoregressive answer decoding with a shared head that scores temporal intervals and textual options against video evidence. These scores yield event spans or answer choices, unifying temporal grounding and multiple-choice video question answering. This combines the semantic flexibility of MLLMs with efficient decisions that agents can use directly. As an interaction unfolds, new goals and intermediate results prompt further queries about the same visual history. VideoJev therefore reuses visual computation through Cached inference for queries as they arrive and Joint inference for multiple queries in a single forward pass. Across three temporal grounding benchmarks, VideoJev-4B and VideoJev-35B-A3B improve mean mIoU over their backbones by 6.7 and 10.8 points, respectively, with measured inference speedups of $2.8$-$3.1\times$. On four video QA benchmarks, both achieve performance comparable to their backbones in Thinking mode, with measured inference speedups exceeding $100\times$. These results offer a unified, reusable decision interface for composing structured visual judgments into complex, open-ended workflows.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 VideoJev，把视频理解与交互建模为结构化决策任务：用共享打分头对时间区间与文本选项打分，替代自回归答案解码，统一时间定位与多选视频问答，并以 Cached 与 Joint 推理复用视觉计算、支持多查询单次前向。
AI.relevance_reason: 以打分头替代 AR 解码、并用缓存/联合推理复用视觉计算，可能为 LVR 中非自回归的推理状态生成与视觉状态缓存复用提供方法线索，可供核查；但原文未涉及 latent 状态的显式构造与使用。
